articles.title: Mill Hill Gets $7,500 for Seasonal Farmers Market
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in January.
body: Organizers say the project is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Thursday mornings. The plan calls for seasonal farmers market along Beacon Avenue, with work expected to start in January.
The group has raised $7,500 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. Felix Kellerman, who has lived in Mill Hill for 37 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.
Public works estimates the work will take about 37 weeks once it begins. The Mill Hill Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.

body: Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Hickory Ridge. Born in Hickory Ridge in the years after the war, Vera Wojcik spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.

articles.title: Then & Now: the Mill Hill Town Hall, 1983 and 2013
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: A 1983 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Linden Street from the corner of Maple Terrace.
Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height.
